Package io.mavlink4j.session

Class MavlinkSession

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.session.MavlinkSession
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class MavlinkSession extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The L3 composition root: one reader thread per registered MavlinkLink, driving that link's own FrameReader and, for every frame it decodes, updating PeerDirectory and LinkHealth, then offering the frame to Correlator and finally to Dispatcher — in that fixed order, never any other. A waiter registered with Correlator.await(io.mavlink4j.session.MatchKey, java.time.Duration) must never miss a reply because a slow Dispatcher handler ran first, which is exactly why Correlator is offered the frame before Dispatcher is.

Ownership

A MavlinkSession does not own the MavlinkLinks registered with it — callers open and close them; removeLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId) and close() stop processing a link (its reader thread exits) without closing the link itself, mirroring FrameWriter.removeLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId)'s own "caller owns that" convention. A registered link's send side is owned here: close() also unregisters every link from the internal FrameWriter.

Threading

addLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.MavlinkLink)/removeLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId)/close() are guarded by one private monitor so they are safe against each other and against the per-link reader threads they start/stop ("one lock protects the registration table"). Each reader thread (named mavlink-rx-<linkId>) is the sole caller of onFrame(io.mavlink4j.codec.Frame) for its own link; PeerDirectory, LinkHealth, Correlator and Dispatcher are all independently safe for concurrent callers from several such threads (a session may register more than one link). close() is idempotent and joins every reader thread bounded by MavlinkSettings.closeJoinTimeout().

A reader thread never blocks indefinitely: MavlinkLink.poll(java.time.Duration) is called with MavlinkSettings.pollTimeout() — purely how often the loop re-checks whether it should stop — so a link that never delivers anything still lets removeLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId)/close() return promptly instead of wedging on a join. Every thread the session starts comes from MavlinkSettings.threadFactory(), and every timestamp it takes from MavlinkSettings.clock().

What the session owns

Besides the registered links' send side, the session owns one TxScheduler (scheduler()) and one LinkQuality (linkQuality()), both closed with it. Services take their scheduler from here instead of building a pool of their own.

    • sendTo

      public void sendTo(Object message, LinkId link, LinkPeer address, PeerId target)
      Sends message to one explicit address on link, bypassing the PeerDirectory. For the one caller that must reach an address the directory has not learned (for example, re-sending a signing key to the address an unsigned vehicle is now heard from); signed with the key target's system resolves to, plain when it has none.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if link is not registered

    • onLinkFailure

      public void onLinkFailure(BiConsumer<LinkId,IOException> listener)
      Registers the listener a reader thread invokes when MavlinkLink.poll(java.time.Duration) throws — a genuine I/O failure, not a timeout or an intentional close (see that method's own contract), and not this session winding down (see below) — instead of runLoop's previous behavior of logging a WARNING and silently returning. At most one listener is meaningful per session; a second call replaces the first rather than chaining, matching every other single-collaborator setter in this codebase.

      Contract the listener must honor Called synchronously from the dying reader thread, inside the same catch block that is about to let that thread exit. The listener must not block — this thread is already unwinding, and a hang here means it never actually exits — and must not throw — any RuntimeException it raises is caught and logged by this class rather than propagating, so a buggy listener cannot itself become a second silent-death path. Do the real work (deciding what "this link is dead" means for a caller — e.g. closing affected publishers exceptionally, D5) on whatever thread the listener hands off to; do not do it inline unless it is already non-blocking.

      Shutdown must not masquerade as failure A link intentionally closed while this session (or the caller) is shutting down must not be reported as a failure — an orderly close()/removeLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId) is not "the radio died". runLoop checks the same MavlinkSession.LinkRuntime.running flag MavlinkSession.LinkRuntime.stop() already sets before ever notifying, rather than inventing a second "are we shutting down" signal: running already answers exactly that question, and it is set (by stop()) before the link is closed, so by the time an intentional close makes MavlinkLink.poll(java.time.Duration) throw — if a particular MavlinkLink ever did that for a close, rather than honoring its own null-on-close contract — running already reads false and this path stays silent, matching a conforming link's own already-silent behavior on close.

    • onFrameRejected

      public void onFrameRejected(Consumer<SignatureRejection> listener)
      Registers the listener a reader thread invokes for every frame SigningPolicy refused -- a frame that was fully decoded but never reached onFrame(io.mavlink4j.codec.Frame) (see SignatureRejection's own javadoc for the two ways that happens). Same single-listener, same calling-thread and no-throw/no-block contract as onLinkFailure(java.util.function.BiConsumer<io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId, java.io.IOException>) — a second call replaces the first, the listener is invoked synchronously from the reader thread that decoded the frame, and any RuntimeException it raises is caught and logged here rather than propagating, so a buggy listener cannot stall or kill that link's reader thread.

    • close

      public void close()
      Idempotent. Stops every reader thread (bounded join), unregisters every link from the sender, then stops the async subscribers and the scheduler.
